sections.html:
Leawood is a long, narrow Johnson County suburb in the southwest corner of the Kansas City area. It covers 15.16 square miles, stretching more than 9 miles north to south and about 2 miles east to west. The state line forms its eastern edge, where it meets eight Kansas City, Missouri neighborhoods. Prairie Village borders it on the north and northwest, Overland Park on the west and south, and the city is divided into four wards.

About 75 percent of the land is developed, so most Leawood houses are already built and sellers compete with other resale homes more than with new lots. Census counts were 27,656 in 2000, 31,867 in 2010 and 33,902 in 2020, with 6.4 percent growth in the last decade.

Leawood ranks among the wealthiest suburbs in the metro, Hallbrook and Mission Hill Estates being typical. Houses at that level are expected to show well, and bringing an older house up to standard is where many owners lose time.

Modern Leawood began in the 1920s, when Oscar G. Lee moved to Johnson County and oversaw the building of Lee Boulevard. The city carries his name. A Kroh Brothers housing development led to incorporation on November 30, 1948, when Leawood was a third-class city with fewer than 2,000 people. It became a second-class city by 1959 and a first-class city by 2014.

The Kroh Brothers modeled their neighborhoods on those of Kansas City developer J. C. Nichols: curving streets, uniform architecture, extensive deed restrictions and homes associations. That is why so many subdivisions still sit under recorded covenants. The covenants and the association's rules go with the house when you sell, and a buyer or title company will ask for them.

Most Leawood neighborhoods have a homes association, so city rules and association rules both apply. The city's Neighborhood Services office enforces a Property Maintenance Code covering premise condition, paint, roof overhangs, gutters and exterior structure condition.

The residential code also lets a legally constituted homes association file a written request with the city's Building Official, giving it a formal role when exterior work is proposed. Before you hire anyone, check both sides, because work done without approval can turn into a violation notice that follows the house.

  • Call Leawood code staff before replacing a roof, fence or exterior features.
  • Ask the association whether the work needs architectural approval.
  • Get dues, transfer fees and any open assessments in writing for the buyer.
  • Confirm whether the house sits in one association or in several overlapping groups.

Closings on listed houses often slip because someone skipped one of these. A cash sale sidesteps most of that prep, though the association may still need a transfer notice.

Leawood is a professional-services and office suburb more than an industrial one. Larger employers include the AMC Theatres Support Center with 450 employees, Reece & Nichols with 415, the American Academy of Family Physicians with 362 and Blue Valley Unified School District with 346. Town Center Plaza is the main shopping center. Employer lists change, and Select Quote cut to fewer than 50 local staff after layoffs in 2024.

A short commute to the rest of the metro means a house here may draw buyers moving for a job in the Kansas City area. Blue Valley USD 229 and the Shawnee Mission School District both serve parts of Leawood. Your street address decides which, and families ask early, so name the right one in your listing notes. The Johnson County Library serves residents, and the police department, formed January 18, 1949, has about 60 officers today.

sections.h2: How Johnson County taxes a Leawood home
sections.html:
Real estate tax in Leawood comes from Johnson County, which bills and collects it, while the County Clerk sets mill levies for each local taxing authority. A mill is 1/1000 of a dollar, so one mill on $1,000 of assessed value is $1.00 in tax. The appraiser's calendar sets the year's rhythm:

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for the appraisal roll
On or before March 1Notices of Appraised Value mailed
On or before March 31Appeal deadline, 30 days from mailing the notice
November 15Tax bills mailed to owners
December 20First half or full tax payment due

For residential property, part of the assessed value is exempt from the 20-mill school general levy. The county lists 8,625 of assessed value exempt for tax years 2024 and 2025, a credit of $172.50. Because Kansas taxes are paid in arrears, a spring sale means asking the title company how the year's bill will be divided.

sections.h2: Deed recording for a Leawood sale
sections.html:
The Johnson County Register of Deeds in Olathe, at 111 S. Cherry Street, Suite 1200, handles recording. Walk-in service runs on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., mail works too, and email or fax does not.

State law (K.S.A. 28-115) sets the charge at $21.00 for page one and $17.00 for each further page. Title companies typically file electronically via an approved vendor. To add a beneficiary to a house you own, a Transfer on Death deed must be signed and notarized before recording and carries the same page fees.

sections.h2: What are the options for selling a Leawood house?
sections.html:
Agent listing, private sale or cash offer: in an established suburb with association rules, the real differences are time, repairs and certainty.

  • A listing fits a well-kept house when you have time to prepare it and wait.
  • Selling privately avoids a fee and leaves the paperwork and association documents in your hands.
  • Cash works for an inherited house, a divorce, a relocation or a property that needs updating.

Leawood houses are something we buy as is. Ask for an offer and compare it with what a listing would net once repairs, dues, taxes and carrying costs come out.

sections.h2: A cash sale, step by step
sections.html:
The first step is an address and a few words about the house, including any association. Next we view it as it stands and send a written offer. If you agree, a title company searches the record and drafts the deed. You then set the closing date.

Expect the buyer or title company to ask for the covenants, so have them ready. Before closing, collect the association contact, a current dues statement and any city notices about exterior work. Dues, transfer fees and open violation notices still run through the title company, even when no repairs are made.

faqs.q: Do Leawood homeowners associations affect a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. Most Leawood neighborhoods have associations, so dues, transfer fees and covenants usually need to be disclosed to the buyer. Ask the association for a current statement early, and check whether more than one group covers your address.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half or full amount is due on or before December 20. Johnson County mails real estate tax bills around November 15, and the appraiser mails valuation notices on or before March 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Leawood property valuation?
faqs.a: The deadline is 30 days after the Notice of Appraised Value is mailed, which is on or before March 31 on the county's calendar.

faqs.q: Which school district is Leawood in?
faqs.a: Leawood is served by two public districts, Blue Valley USD 229 and the Shawnee Mission School District. Which one applies depends on the street address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Leawood house in an association without making repairs first?
faqs.a: A cash buyer purchases as is, so cosmetic or deferred repairs do not need to be done before closing. Association dues, transfer fees and any open violation notices from the city still need to be disclosed and settled through the title company.
